verdict: GitHub Copilot: Choose GitHub Copilot when AI coding inside GitHub and your current IDE is the job — not Microsoft 365 Copilot. Scores use the AI editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Lives in GitHub and major IDEs
Unlimited completions on paid plans (per GitHub billing docs)
weaknesses: AI Credit overage after included pool
Enterprise SKU tied to GitHub Enterprise Cloud

Easy to confuse with Microsoft 365 Copilot in procurement
bestFor: Teams already on GitHub who want IDE + PR Copilot
Orgs that need Business/Enterprise policy on a familiar SKU
Developers who want completions without switching editors
notIdealFor: Buyers whose job is Microsoft 365 drafting (M365 Copilot)
Developers standardised on an AI-native editor (Cursor)
tradeoffs: Published free tiers vs paid usage/credit caps
Bundled Workspace/One plans vs standalone assistant pricing
Credit/overage models vs predictable seat pricing
Enterprise admin controls vs individual consumer plans
recommendation: Choose GitHub Copilot when AI coding inside GitHub and your current IDE is the job — not Microsoft 365 Copilot. Compare Cursor for an AI-native editor; ChatGPT if you only need general coding chat.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Installs into VS Code/JetBrains/github.com with little new surface — strong for GitHub-native teams.
Primary job is AI coding assistant — ranked in ai-code with Cursor, not as an LLM-assistant peer of ChatGPT.
Completions and chat quality track GitHub’s model catalog; not a hands-on bake-off vs Cursor.
PR, repo, and cloud-agent workflows add depth beyond autocomplete; held at 8 vs AI-native IDEs.
Native GitHub + IDE plugins is the distribution advantage.
Business/Enterprise publish org policy and admin; consumer Pro is weaker.

Broad model catalog on paid plans; not claimed as the single highest-compute IDE.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine AI editorial criteria using category weights (AI job fit 16, output quality 14, ease of use 12, workflow depth 12, integrations 10, governance/privacy 10, value 10, model capability 8, scalability 8), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — LLM assistants, writing, voice, presentations, websites, ad creative, and agent builders are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
